displayedInputs.question: A tank has a capacity of 60 m³. A pump fills it at a rate of v m³/h, and the time needed to fill it is t h. If the tank must be filled within 4 hours (\(t\le4\)), what is the minimum filling rate v in m³/h?
A high-speed train travels at 300 km/h. Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the distance s km and the time t needed to travel that distance? (The unit of t is h.)
How many hours does a high-speed train need to travel 900 km at 300 km/h?
A high-speed railway line is 780 km long. If the average speed increases from 260 km/h to 312 km/h, by how many hours does the total travel time decrease? (You may give a decimal.)

Two places are 600 km apart. The travel time t (h) and average speed v (km/h) of a high-speed train satisfy \(t=600/v\). If the travel time must not exceed 2.5 h, what is the minimum average speed in km/h?
Point A is rotated clockwise through \(90^\circ\) about O to obtain A′. What is the relationship between OA and OA′?
Which three elements are needed to determine a rotation?

choices.A: Center of rotation, radius of rotation, duration of rotation
choices.B: Center of rotation, direction of rotation, angle of rotation
choices.C: Axis of symmetry, direction of rotation, angle of rotation
choices.D: Center of rotation, corresponding points, axis of symmetry

displayedInputs.question: Point O is the center of rotation. Point A is rotated about O to obtain A′. Given \(OA=5\) and \(\angle AOA'=90^\circ\), find the square of AA′ (that is, the value of \(AA'^2\)).
Triangle ABC is rotated about C to obtain triangle A′B′C, with A′ lying on side AB. Given \(\angle A=70^\circ\), find the angle of rotation \(\angle ACA'\). (Unit: degrees)
What relationships hold between corresponding line segments and corresponding angles before and after a rotation?

choices.A: Corresponding line segments are equal in length, and corresponding angles are equal
choices.B: Corresponding line segments are proportional, and corresponding angles are equal
choices.C: Corresponding line segments are equal in length, and corresponding angles are supplementary

displayedInputs.question: Triangle ABC is rotated about O to obtain triangle A′B′C′. Given \(AB=7\) and \(\angle A=40^\circ\), find the length of A′B′ and the measure of \(\angle A'\) in degrees. (Give the answers in this order, separated by a comma.)
Point P is rotated about the center of rotation O to obtain P′. Given \(OP=5\) and the angle of rotation \(\angle POP'=90^\circ\), find the square of PP′ (that is, the value of \(PP'^2\)).
Triangle ABC is rotated about C to obtain triangle A′B′C, with A′ lying on side AB and \(\angle A=65^\circ\). Find the angle of rotation \(\angle ACA'\). (Unit: degrees)
Triangle ABC is rotated counterclockwise through \(90^\circ\) about C. How do you construct the image of A?

choices.A: Construct a line through A perpendicular to CA, and choose any point on this line as A′
choices.B: Join C to A, construct \(\angle ACA'=90^\circ\), and mark off \(CA'=AB\)
choices.C: Join C to A, construct \(\angle ACA'=90^\circ\) in the counterclockwise direction, and mark off \(CA'=CA\)

displayedInputs.question: Triangle ABC is rotated counterclockwise through \(90^\circ\) about C to obtain triangle A′B′C′. Given \(CA=6\) cm, find the length of CA′. (Unit: cm)

In a Cartesian coordinate system, point \(B(-3,4)\) is rotated clockwise through \(90^\circ\) about the origin O to obtain B′. Find the coordinates of B′. (Give the x-coordinate followed by the y-coordinate, separated by a comma.)

In a Cartesian coordinate system in the plane, point \(P(4,3)\) is rotated \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise about point \(C(1,1)\) to obtain point \(P'\). Find the coordinates of \(P'\) (enter the x-coordinate followed by the y-coordinate, separated by a comma).
In square \(ABCD\), points \(E\) and \(F\) lie on \(BC\) and \(CD\), respectively, and \(\angle EAF=45^\circ\). How can you prove that \(EF=BE+DF\)?

choices.A: Draw a line through \(A\) perpendicular to \(EF\), and prove that \(\triangle ABE\cong\triangle ADF\).
choices.B: Rotate \(\triangle ADF\) through \(90^\circ\) about \(A\) so that \(AD\) coincides with \(AB\), and prove that \(\triangle AEF\cong\triangle AEF'\).
choices.C: Draw \(AC\) and \(BD\), and prove that \(AC\perp BD\).

displayedInputs.question: In square \(ABCD\), rotate \(\triangle ADF\) through \(90^\circ\) about point \(A\) so that \(AD\) coincides with \(AB\). The point corresponding to \(F\) is \(F'\). If \(DF=3\), find the length of \(BF'\).
Square \(ABCD\) has side length \(6\). Points \(E\) and \(F\) lie on \(BC\) and \(CD\), respectively, with \(\angle EAF=45^\circ\), \(BE=2\), and \(DF=3\). Find the length of \(EF\).
Point \(P\) lies inside equilateral triangle \(ABC\), with \(PA=3\), \(PB=4\), and \(PC=5\). Find the measure of \(\angle APB\) (in degrees).
List three centrally symmetric figures. Which of the following groups consists of three centrally symmetric figures?
Points \(A\) and \(A'\) are centrally symmetric about point \(O\). If \(OA=3.5\), find the length of \(AA'\).
Which of the following statements about “central symmetry” and “centrally symmetric figures” is correct?

choices.A: Central symmetry is a relationship between two figures, while being centrally symmetric is a property of a single figure.
choices.B: The two terms have exactly the same meaning, with no difference.
choices.C: A centrally symmetric figure is a figure that coincides with itself after a \(90^\circ\) rotation about a point.

displayedInputs.question: Among these six figures, how many are centrally symmetric: a line segment, an equilateral triangle, a square, a regular pentagon, a circle, and a parallelogram?
What is the point symmetric to \((3,-2)\) about the origin? (Enter the x-coordinate followed by the y-coordinate, separated by a comma.)
What is the point symmetric to \((-4,-7)\) about the origin? (Enter the x-coordinate followed by the y-coordinate, separated by a comma.)
Points \(P(a,3)\) and \(Q(-2,b)\) are symmetric about the origin. Find the value of \(a+b\).
Point \(M(a,b)\) lies in the second quadrant. In which quadrant does its symmetric point about the origin lie?
Points \(P(2m+1,3)\) and \(Q(-5,n-1)\) are symmetric about the origin. Find the value of \(m\cdot n\).
What is the length of the longest chord in a circle of radius \(5\)?
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: Every arc of a circle is a semicircle.
choices.B: A diameter is the longest chord in a circle.
choices.C: Two circles with equal radii are concentric.

displayedInputs.question: The diameter of \(\odot O\) is \(8\), and the length of chord \(AB\) is an integer. How many possible values are there for the length of \(AB\)?
There are \(6\) points on a circle. What is the maximum number of distinct chords that can be obtained by joining any two points?
The radius of \(\odot O\) is \(10\), and the distance from the center to chord \(AB\) is \(6\). Find the length of chord \(AB\).
Chord \(AB\) of \(\odot O\) has length \(AB=24\). The distance from the center \(O\) to \(AB\) is \(5\). Find the radius of \(\odot O\).
Which statement about the perpendicular diameter theorem and its corollaries is correct?

choices.A: A diameter that bisects a chord (that is not a diameter) is perpendicular to that chord.
choices.B: A line that bisects a chord must be perpendicular to that chord.
choices.C: A line perpendicular to a chord must pass through the center of the circle.

displayedInputs.question: The radius of \(\odot O\) is \(5\). Chord \(AB\parallel\) chord \(CD\), \(AB=6\), and \(CD=8\). The two chords lie on opposite sides of the center \(O\). Find the distance between \(AB\) and \(CD\).
In the same circle, how are the arcs and chords subtended by equal central angles related?

choices.A: The arcs are equal, but the chords are not necessarily equal.
choices.B: The arcs are equal, and the chords are equal.
choices.C: The chords are equal, but the arcs are not necessarily equal.

displayedInputs.question: In a circle with center \(O\), \(\angle AOB=\angle COD=50^\circ\), and chord \(AB=6\). Find the length of chord \(CD\).
